input: Write morning journal entries for 30 days

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Morning journaling can mean very different things — free writing, structured prompts, gratitude lists, brain dumps — and knowing what is included shapes the entire plan.
Is this purely personal, or will entries be shared with a therapist, coach, partner, or audience? An audience changes tone and privacy considerations.
Whether this starts today or on a fixed future date, and what existing morning routine it fits into, determines the scheduling and habit-stacking strategy.
How much time the user has each morning sets the realistic length and depth of each entry — 5 minutes is very different from 30 minutes.
The underlying purpose — mental clarity, emotional processing, creativity, productivity, self-discovery — changes what themes, prompts, or frameworks to use.
Whether journaling happens on paper, a notes app, a dedicated journal app, or a doc affects format, templates, and how entries are stored or reviewed.
Knowing what success looks like — consistency streak, noticeable mood shift, a completed archive, specific insights — determines how to track progress and what to measure.

gold.taskTitle: Write 30 Days of Morning Journal Entries
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to establish or complete a 30-day morning journaling practice, writing an entry each day.

questions.title: What is the main purpose behind your journaling?
questions.description: Understanding the core goal — e.g., mental clarity, emotional processing, creativity, gratitude, self-discovery — determines which themes and frameworks to build the 30-day arc around.

questions.title: What format do you want each entry to follow?
questions.description: Clarifies whether entries are free-form stream of consciousness, structured prompts, bullet points, a specific method like Morning Pages or the 5-Minute Journal, or something else entirely.

questions.title: How many minutes can you dedicate each morning?
questions.description: The available time window determines realistic entry length and depth, and whether the habit needs to be kept very short or can be more expansive.

questions.title: Which tool or medium will you write in?
questions.description: Knowing whether the user will use a physical notebook, a notes app, a dedicated journaling app, or a document influences formatting, templates, and review strategies.

questions.title: When do you plan to start your 30-day streak?
questions.description: Pinning down the start date and how it fits into an existing morning routine allows for concrete scheduling and habit-stacking recommendations.

questions.title: Are these entries private or meant to be shared?
questions.description: Whether the journal is entirely personal or intended for a therapist, coach, or public audience directly affects how honest, polished, or audience-aware each entry needs to be.

questions.title: What would make this 30-day challenge feel successful?
questions.description: Defining the desired outcome — a completed streak, a mood shift, captured insights, a finished document — shapes how progress is tracked and what milestones to celebrate.
